title: iPhone Video Audio Drifts Out of Sync After Import?
description: Test for variable frame rate when iPhone video audio drifts out of sync after import. Compare early and late cues on one steady-rate copy.
direct: Compare the first and last visible sound cues. If only the editor drifts, test one constant-frame-rate export against both cues.
figureAlt: A film maker performing a hand clap in front of a tripod-mounted iPhone at a home studio desk
cards.decision.heading: Check two audible events
cards.decision.body: Look for a clap, a drum hit or a visible consonant near each end. If the original camera audio lines up early but drifts late, check how your editor handles the clip’s timestamps. Test with camera audio alone first.
sections.detail-1.heading: If the clip came from an HDR recording
sections.detail-1.body: Check color separately if the source is HDR. Use the clap to compare sync first. If your project needs HDR delivery, verify the color of any test export before you replace source media.
sections.detail-2.heading: About the app
sections.detail-2.body: Space Sheep Studio develops this iPhone app. Check the App Store listing for current access and export options.
faqs.first-question.heading: Will steady frame rate fix every sync issue?
faqs.first-question.body: No. It tests one source of drift. If both files drift, check the editor settings or the source recording.
faqs.second-question.heading: What if sound is late by the same amount throughout?
faqs.second-question.body: That is a fixed offset. Align one clear cue and confirm a second cue before re-encoding.

steps.step-1.text: Play the source in Photos and compare an early and a late cue.
steps.step-2.text: In VideoFix, make one steady frame-rate copy. Choose the frame rate appropriate for your timeline.
steps.step-3.text: Import both files into a fresh timeline. Compare both cues before processing the rest.
